title: Value containing backslash followed by ';' or '#' does not round-trip
property: parse(stringify(obj)) deep-equals obj for string values
actual: {a:'\\'} (the ';' is treated as a comment start)
evidence: stringify escapes ';' and '#' with a backslash but does not escape a preceding backslash, so the output 'a=\\;' is read by parse as an escaped backslash followed by an unescaped comment marker. encode/decode are a documented inverse pair, and safe() exists to make values round-trippable.

title: Single-quote character value parses as empty string
evidence: safe() guards its quote check with val.length > 1, so a lone "'" is emitted unquoted, but unsafe()'s isQuoted has no length check: a single quote both starts and ends with "'", so slice(1,-1) yields ''. The two halves are inconsistent.
